== WHAT I FOUND FIRST (this changes the shape of the answer) ==

`--json` is not a new idea in this repo. It was already considered and explicitly declined. `docs/plans/PLAN-gate-usability.md`, Open questions: "`--json` output for scripting? Leaning **no**, speculative until asked." And in its Implementation

Asked to re-pad \"Gates:\" and \"Stage:\" from three spaces to four so they would \"align at four\". I verified the premise before acting and found it false, so I changed nothing and reported why.\n\nMeasured facts (from hooks/status.js plus its rendered output): \"Gates:\" and \"Stage:\" are 6-character labels with 3 spaces of padding; \"File:\" and \"Note:\" are 5-character labels with 4 spaces; every continuation line is indented 9 spaces. All four labels and all eleven continuation lines therefore place their value at column 10. The padding varies precisely BECAUSE the label lengths vary -

ANSWER — Why the BOM is stripped before parsing.\n\nCursor prefixes every hook payload it sends over stdin with a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF). `JSON.parse` throws on that leading character, so a hook written the obvious way — parse, inspect, decide — catches the exception, decides nothing, and exits 0. The result is a gate that looks installed, logs no error, and silently allows everything: it fails open. The repo calls this undocumented behavior \"the single most dangerous defect found while building this\" / \"the most dangerous finding of the whole exercise\", and notes it also passes every test wri

ROUTING ANSWER

(a) "node --test <dir> fails because Node resolves the directory as a module path" -> CLAUDE.md's ## Gotchas section.

Why: it passes the repo's own decision test (CLAUDE.md lines 186-188) as a defensive warning -- phrasable as "Don't run node --test <dir>". It is reactive (alerts to a footgun at the moment you type the command), fits one line, and needs to be in always-loaded context to help, because the mistake happens before anyone would think to consult a topical file.

Important finding: this gotcha is ALREADY RECORDED, at C:\Users\kobiv\Projects\claude-basic

The glob is quoted so Node expands it rather than the shell, keeping the command identical on Windows and Linux.
